pr_body:
When `PEM_write_bio_PKCS8PrivateKey()` and `PEM_write_bio_PKCS8PrivateKey_nid()`
were passed empty passphrase strings, `OPENSSL_memdup()` was incorrectly getting
used for 0 bytes size allocations, which resulted in malloc failures.

Fixes: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/17506

Signed-off-by: Darshan Sen <raisinten@gmail.com>

pr_comments: In general this is wrong place to fix your problem. This needs to be properly handled at the callers to not try 0 bytes size allocation or memory duplication.

> In general this is wrong place to fix your problem. This needs to be properly handled at the callers to not try 0 bytes size allocation or memory duplication.

@t8m thanks, updated accordingly.
The CI failures are relevant.

@t8m it's just the callback variation that fails which was happening even before this change was added. I'm suspecting that's happening due to an incorrect invocation of the API? (suggestions would be great!) I've commented out that test for now with a TODO. If CI passes now (not sure why these tests aren't run for me locally, will investigate later) and y'all are good with the change, I'll try to sign the CLA.
Please re-enable the last test case. The error can be fixed by changing https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/master/crypto/ui/ui_util.c#L117 to `if (len < 0)`
Also please sign and send the CLA.

> Please re-enable the last test case. The error can be fixed by changing https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/master/crypto/ui/ui_util.c#L117 to `if (len < 0)`

but please be careful, return values 0 and -1 have a special meaning,
and the user callback has no way to return 0 any more with this change.
this is the caller:
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/5288303da96084b41b062d99eb37177fb4cf471e/crypto/ui/ui_lib.c#L516-L530
and this is the callee:
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/5288303da96084b41b062d99eb37177fb4cf471e/crypto/ui/ui_util.c#L111-L121

Well, I just said one should be very careful, when changing
the meaning of the return value of any user callback.

I am also nervous about this:
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/f59d72f027da90edcccad5cc78c94d3099fadecf/crypto/pem/pem_pk8.c#L138-L142

It would be better to change this too, and more importantly also have
test coverage for this code path.

But, what worries me, is when I look at the function `i2d_PKCS8PrivateKey_bio`
this made me think that currently a user callback can return an error by
returning 0 or -1 here.  Likewise the pem_callback currently can return 0
to raise a hard error, while return -1 means something like user abort.
So there is a subtle difference in the error handling.
Probably we loose a way to signal a hard error from the user callback.

> Well, I just said one should be very careful, when changing the meaning of the return value of any user callback.

But we are not changing it! We are correcting the mistake at the callers.

If you look at the implementation of PEM_def_callback which is the default implementation of this pem_password_cb() and if you look at the example of the pem_password_cb implementation at the manual page you can clearly see that returning 0 means zero length password and not and error! Citation from the manual page: `The callback must return the number of characters in the passphrase or -1 if an error occurred.`

> I am also nervous about this:

This is just another bug - the condition should be `if (klen < 0)` if we want/can support 0 length passwords there.

> But, what worries me, is when I look at the function `i2d_PKCS8PrivateKey_bio`

And that's another place where 0 byte passwords are unsupported. Which does not necessarily mean they cannot be. I can only repeat the manual page says fairly explicitly that just -1 is an error.

@t8m I changed the `<=` to `<` like you asked me to, let's see if CI passes this time! Is there any chance I can sign the CLA without taking a printout of https://www.openssl.org/policies/openssl_icla.pdf? May I add a picture of my signature instead like how docusign works?

Can you please also look at changing this one:
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/f59d72f027da90edcccad5cc78c94d3099fadecf/crypto/pem/pem_pk8.c#L138-L142

and can someone figure out a way how that can be executed?

> and can someone figure out a way how that can be executed?

That would be executed for a legacy pkey I suppose.

> May I add a picture of my signature instead like how docusign works?

Yes, that is acceptable.

> Can you please also look at changing this one:
> 
> https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/f59d72f027da90edcccad5cc78c94d3099fadecf/crypto/pem/pem_pk8.c#L138-L142
> 
> and can someone figure out a way how that can be executed?

@bernd-edlinger This can only de done through `PEM_write_bio_PKCS8PrivateKey_nid()`. Added a second commit to apply the fix you mentioned and added tests too but it fails because `p8` is assigned a null value here:
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/e1cd94f2dca4056ce042c62b89c468dffc088033/crypto/pem/pem_pk8.c#L146
Not sure where I should make a change to fix this. 🤔

> Yes, that is acceptable.

@t8m thanks, signed the CLA :)

For your new test, You have to use one of the NIDs listed here:
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/e1cd94f2dca4056ce042c62b89c468dffc088033/crypto/evp/evp_pbe.c#L36-L65

For instance `NID_pbe_WithSHA1And3_Key_TripleDES_CBC` should work.
@bernd-edlinger thanks, that fixed the test failure, PTAL :)
This pull request is ready to merge
Merged to master and 3.0 branches (resolving the CHANGES.md conflict manually). Thank you for your contribution.

issue_context.title: `PEM_write_bio_PKCS8PrivateKey()` doesn't accept empty passphrase strings anymore
issue_context.body:
At Node.js, in order to pass an empty passphrase string to `PEM_write_bio_PKCS8PrivateKey()` without running the default callback which unwantedly opens up a user input prompt, we were passing these variables:
```cc
char* kstr = reinterpret_cast<char*>(-1)
size_t klen = 0
```
This was working okay up to 1.1.1l but from 3.0.1, we started noticing some unexpected malloc failures.

I found the cause of the malloc failure:
* https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/71396cd048072b69559b46d98cfebfd4474cd712/crypto/o_str.c#L55-L59
Along with the return value of `CRYPTO_malloc()` being `NULL`, `errno` too should be checked for an `ENOMEM` value to consider this to be a malloc failure.
* https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/71396cd048072b69559b46d98cfebfd4474cd712/crypto/passphrase.c#L43-L48
Along with the return value of `OPENSSL_memdup()` being `NULL`, `errno` too should be checked for an `ENOMEM` value to consider this to be a malloc failure.

I tried fixing those locally but now I get:
```js
[Error: error:07880106:common libcrypto routines::passed invalid argument] {
  opensslErrorStack: [ 'error:1C80009F:Provider routines::unable to get passphrase' ],
  library: 'common libcrypto routines',
  reason: 'passed invalid argument',
  code: 'ERR_OSSL_CRYPTO_PASSED_INVALID_ARGUMENT'
}
```

Locally I had also tried passing a custom callback as a workaround:
```cc
auto pass_cb = [](char *buf, int size, int rwflag, void *u) -> int {
  return 0;
};
```
but that fails with:
```js
[Error: error:14000065:UI routines::result too small] {
  opensslErrorStack: [
    'error:1C80009F:Provider routines::unable to get passphrase',
    'error:07880109:common libcrypto routines::interrupted or cancelled',
    'error:0480006D:PEM routines::problems getting password',
    'error:1400006B:UI routines::processing error'
  ],
  library: 'UI routines',
  reason: 'result too small',
  code: 'ERR_OSSL_UI_RESULT_TOO_SMALL'
}
```

Bug report in the Node.js repo: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/41428
Relevant code area in Node.js: https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/426df1b836432bb6c4dd2beb127d40d804db7aeb/src/crypto/crypto_keys.cc#L292-L390

comments: PR to fix the invalid malloc failure reports: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/17507

I wonder if an empty passphrase is valid at all.
You cannot enter it with `-password pass:` for instance.
When entering from the console you have to enter 4 letters min.

Aehm, disregard my comment about less than 4 letter password, that is a pkcs12 feature.
pkcs8 accepts even empty passwords...

review_comments: and I wonder if a negative test, where the callback return -1 would make sense too.
Yes, that would make sense to add.

Most other places where NID_pbe_WithSHA1And3_Key_TripleDES_CBC are used,
are guarded with `#ifndef OPENSSL_NO_DES`.  I guess it would be better to try that
only if the DES cipher is available
